tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

Cleaner: keep `boot` returning `Future<void>` and hold run in a field? The tests do `final run = await boot(cli)` — with boot returning `run` (a Future) awaited by the OUTER await → double-await problem! `await boot(cli)` awaits boot, which returns `run` — if boot's return type is Future<Future<void>>... I declared Future<void> with `return run` — Dart flattens: `await boot` waits for BOTH readiness and run completion?? No — `return run` inside an `async` function FLATTENS: boot completes only when run completes. BAD — that would deadlock (run waits for /exit which we send after boot). Fix: make boot return the run future without awaiting: `Future<Future<void>> boot(...) async {...; return run;}` then `final run = await boot(cli);` gives the unawaited run future.

::group::❌ IT-4/REG-2: the 2026-10-22 incident replay fails closed (AC4) mixed boot + picker pick of kimi-for-coding + message never produces a copilot-endpoint request carrying kimi-for-coding (failed)
TimeoutException after 0:00:30.000000: Test timed out after 30 seconds. See https://pub.dev/packages/test#timeouts
dart:isolate  _RawReceivePort._handleMessage
::endgroup::

::error::0 tests passed, 1 failed.

content.thinking:
Timeout somewhere in IT-4. The waits: boot ✓ (same fixture as IT-1 typed which passes), tuiSelectModelForTest('kimi|kimi-for-coding') → waitForIt(id=='kimi-for-coding') — this passes in the picker test... Then `statusProviderLabelForTest()` — sync. Then `_lastModelChangeProvider(env)` — walker... then sendLine('are you coherent?') → `waitForIt(() => !cli.isBusy && fake.calls == 1)` — THE MESSAGE TURN. In the other tests fake.calls stays 0 — here I EXPECT a call. The turn: `fake.call` is the injected streamFunction — wait, in IT-4 the wiring after `_switchProvider` — LEGACY branch — `_streamFunction = _catalogStreamFunction(kimi kind, key)` → `providerStreamFunction('openai-completions','kimi-key')` — THE REAL ADAPTER, not the fake!! IT-4 didn't pass catalogStreamOverride — the fixture injects `streamFunction: fake.call` but `_switchProvider` OVERWRITES `_agent.streamFunction = _streamFunction` (the real catalog stream). So the message turn goes to the REAL openai-completions adapter → real http POST to api.kimi.com → hangs/times out → fake.calls never 1.

Fix: IT-4 must ride `catalogStreamOverride: (kind, key) => fake.call` instead of the injected streamFunction — then `_catalogStreamFunction` wraps and inner = fake. Build IT-4's cli with `catalogStreamOverride` and NO streamFunction. The incidentCli fixture always passes streamFunction — add a flag `rideCatalogStream` to the fixture: when true, pass catalogStreamOverride and omit streamFunction.

Tool error (bash): # crap4dart configuration for flutter_agent_harness.
# https://github.com/IstiN/crap4dart
#
# RATCHET: the CRAP threshold is pinned at the current worst score
# (356.34, `_handleKey` in bin/../tui_repl.dart) — pushes may only make
# the codebase BETTER, never worse. Lower the threshold whenever the top
# offenders are fixed (run: dart pub global run crap4dart analyze).

sources: [lib, bin]

exclude:
  - '**.g.dart'
  - '**.freezed.dart'
  - '**.mocks.dart'
  - 'build/**'
  - 'vendor/**'

crap:
  enabled: true
  # Current max CRAP score in the repo: 12.0 (re-measured whole-tree on
  # the merged-suite lcov, #1234 rework). The card's named offenders DID
  # move — readPasteboardImage 16.32 (split into fake-seam /
  # platform-dispatch helpers), the CC-12 trio (_handleTreeKey,
  # discoverTaskAgents, _rebuild) split into cohesive sub-dispatchers,
  # the four 0%-cov CC-3 methods covered by tests (frontmatter, video
  # endpoint, below-window ingest, provider picker), the named CC-9 tier
  # split, and _listModels (20 @ 0%) covered by the line-mode /models
  # test. But the FIRST real whole-tree measurement (the authoring box
  # had no dart toolchain) shows the 12.0 → 8.0 repin is not earned yet:
  # 137 methods measure above 8.0 — 54 at exactly 12.00 (the CC-3 @ 0%
  # tier + fully-covered CC-12 dispatchers) and 83 at 9.00 (CC-9 @ 100%).
  # Threshold stays at the measured max; the 12.00/9.00 tier is the next
  # ladder card (cover the CC-3@0% half, split the CC-12 dispatchers,
  # then the threshold follows down to 8.0). Only down from here.
  # TEMP raise (crap4dart 0.11.0 -> 0.14.2 migration, PR #1637, re-opens the
  # gh-1234 repin under the new analyzer): 0.14.2 counts pattern-matching /
  # switch complexity higher, re-measuring the provider-queue cluster above
  # the old 12.0 line. Measured on the CI pipeline (core coverage shards of
  # run 39324246012, merged via scripts/merge_lcov.py, analyze lib bin):
  # max CRAP 90.00 (`_typeName`, providers_queue.dart:629, CC 9 @ 0% cov),
  # then 35.00 (`BindingProvenance.label`, provider_model_binding.dart:69,
  # CC 8 @ 25%). Restore to 12.0 by decomposing the cluster under 0.14.2.
  # raise-issue: gh-1713
  # Restored (gh-1713 round 2, 2026-10-21): _typeName 90→9 (0%-cov pure
  # name-table — now covered by the type-naming parse-error group in
  # test/model_roles/providers_queue_test.dart, all seven arms) and
  # BindingProvenance.label 35→1 (the switch duplicated the enum name arm
  # for arm; the getter is `=> name`, CC 1, coverage-independent). The
  # threshold follows back down 90.0 → 12.0 — the gh-1234 line restored.
  # Only down.
  threshold: 12.0
  # _listModels used to hit 20 with 0% coverage (line-mode-only output);
  # covered by test/cli/provider_models_line_mode_test.dart in #1234.

# ─── loc gate (issue #1234, gh-1232 migration) ─────────────────────────────
# The ≤2800-line file guard MOVED from scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_size +
# the ci.yml shell find-exec guards onto crap4dart's `loc` gate (0.11.0,
# maintainer-confirmed wc -l semantics). Enforced whole-tree on every merge
# validation via `crap4dart check --baseline` (CI quality-gates step) and
# staged files in the pre-commit hook — no staged-scoping escape, no
# hook-dependence, merge-bot merges included. max_lines only DOWN;
# app_localizations.dart is gen-l10n OUTPUT (no .g.dart suffix) — excluded,
# not baselined.

coverage:
  # scripts/pre-commit regenerates this (dart test --coverage) right
  # before the CRAP step runs.
  lcov_path: coverage/lcov.info
  required: true
  branch_coverage: true
  # crap4dart 0.9.5 flipped the run_tests default to true — a bare
  # `analyze`/`check` would silently re-run the whole core suite first.
  # Coverage is regenerated explicitly (pre-commit hook, CI shard merge);
  # do not pay for it twice.
  run_tests: false

# ─── Gates (issue #447) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 0.9.5 default-enables ALL built-in gates; only broken_goldens is
# enforced here, everything else is disabled explicitly so a bare
# `check --staged` (pre-commit, core-only #433 split) means exactly the
# pixel gate. The flutter_app goldens live in flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.
gates:
  # Issue #1234: the whole-tree ≤2800-line guard (was stage_size +
  # ci.yml shell find-exec, gh-1232). wc -l semantics, generated output
  # excluded — nothing exceeds 2800 today, so the shrink-only baseline
  # starts EMPTY of loc entries. Scope = the package sources [lib, bin]:
  # 0.11.0 has NO per-gate sources override (gates.loc.sources is a
  # ConfigException — caught by CI on 019ede65), and the top-level
  # sources drive the CRAP census too, so they stay untouched. test/ and
  # example/ are enforced by the companion config
  # crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml (same loc gate, sources [test, example]);
  # the app package's own config covers flutter_app/lib.
  loc:
    enabled: true
    max_lines: 2800
    exclude:
      - '**.g.dart'
      - '**.freezed.dart'
      - '**.mocks.dart'
      - 'vendor/**'
  test_coverage: {enabled: false} # own ≥80% coverage-gate job
  complexity: {enabled: false} # CRAP ratchet above already covers it
  method_size: {enabled: false}
  nesting: {enabled: false}
  class_size: {enabled: false}
  weight_of_class: {enabled: false}
  unused_code: {enabled: false}
  unused_files: {enabled: false} # follow-up card (issue #1234 §5). Known
    # FPs to exclude when enabling: the conditional-export IO entry points
    # (lib/io.dart, lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart — public barrels whose
    # importers live outside this repo's import graph) and shared pinned
    # data modules imported only from test/ (lib/src/cli/omp_reg_scenarios.dart,
    # issue #810). lib/fanet.dart was the one confirmed-dead hit — deleted
    # in #1234.
  banned_imports: {enabled: false}
  # Type-2 duplication gate (issue #1106, crap4dart 0.11.0). Renamed-clone
  # detection on top of the Type-1 default; the union with the raw pass can
  # only ADD findings, never lose exact copies. severity: warning starts
  # soft — escalate to error once the 13-file triage debt is paid
  # (follow-up, owner-side). The global jscpd <1% guards stay as-is.
  #
  # Two suppression channels with different contracts:
  # - `// crap:ignore` (needs ignorable: true) = a JUSTIFIED structural
  #   twin, suppressed forever, with a one-line reason in the comment.
  # - `.crap-baseline.json` (via `check --baseline`) = LEGACY debt; the
  #   committed snapshot must only SHRINK: after each triage batch re-run
  #   `dart pub global run crap4dart check --save-baseline` and commit the
  #   only-down diff, or the snapshot rots and starts masking shifts.
  #
  # WINDOW (until severity flips to error): the gate never fails a build —
  # new (not-baselined) duplication only surfaces as a `[WARN]` line in
  # `check` output. Enforcement becomes hard exactly when the owner-side
  # escalation lands; from then on any finding outside the two channels
  # fails CI/pre-commit.
  duplication:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    ignorable: true # enables `// crap:ignore` for justified structural twins
    ignore_locals: true # Type-2: rename locals before hashing (API names stay)
    ignore_literals: false # keeps l10n/theme/symbol tables out
    sources: # cross-module scope from #487
      - flutter_app/lib
      - packages/fa_ui/lib
      - packages/fa_llm/lib
  file_naming: {enabled: false}
  magic_constants: {enabled: false}
  test_assertions: {enabled: false}
  folder_structure: {enabled: false}
  external: {enabled: false}
  public_docs: {enabled: false}
  golden: {enabled: false} # flutter-only gate (core is not a Flutter project)
  accessibility: {enabled: false}
  hardcoded_strings: {enabled: false}

  # Pixel gate over core test/ goldens — none exist today, so this is a
  # no-op that guards the future (issue #447 AC: "and core test/ goldens
  # if any appear"). ERROR since crap4dart >=0.14.2 fixed the upstream
  # detector bugs (checkmark V, yellow-on-dark digits, hollow-box
  # ambiguity) — scripts/check_golden_detector.py --expect-fixed is the
  # flip gate and it is MET.
  broken_goldens:
    enabled: true
    severity: error
    dirs: [test]
    exclude:
      # TUI screenshots, not goldens: terminal text is blocky mono
      # glyphs that read as solid Ahem rectangles (5 theme screenshots,
      # crap4dart 0.14.2), and omp_ref/03_tool_call.png genuinely
      # contains a yellow/black pattern. Not golden images — excluded,
      # not a detector bug to chase.
      - 'test/integration/**'

  # File-level near-duplicate gate (issue #1738, crap4dart 0.15.0).
  # Guard rails from the measured inventory on this repo (3498 scanned →
  # exactly the card's 25 files / 12 clusters after the excludes below):
  # only NEW near-duplicates fail — the historical clusters live in
  # .crap-baseline.json (via `check --save-baseline`), here is WHY each
  # stays, not fixed in this card:
  #   test/ci_*_upload_retry_guard_test triple — sibling CI-shard retry
  #     guards; shared scaffolding to extract (follow-up triage debt).
  #   flutter_app/integration_test/{bash,edit}_tool_test — card-named
  #     shared integration scaffolding.
  #   test/integration/provider_{ollama,openrouter}_test — card-named
  #     shared provider scaffolding (the anthropic leg drifted below
  #     threshold since the card's measurement).
  #   flutter_app/lib/network/ws_connector_{io,web} — platform-split
  #     twins (conditional-export io/web halves of one connector).
  #   flutter_app/lib/services/{folder,upload}_picker_web — platform
  #     twins, same pattern, one web picker family.
  #   app_preflight_probe_io ⇄ test/native_test_guard — the probe and
  #     its native-test guard share the probe script by design.
  #   media_slot_picker_page / provider_registry tests across
  #     flutter_app ⇄ packages/fa_ui — drifted cross-package test
  #     siblings (containment 1.00 on provider_registry: the fa_ui copy
  #     is a superset; unifying is a refactor card).
  #   {transformers_js,webllm}_cache_section tests + the two no_tools
  #     prompt notes — provider twins differing by provider name;
  #     parameterizing the notes/generators is the prompt-corpus
  #     refactor card (gh-1738 sanctioned baseline-with-comment here).
  #   test/cli/agent_cli_tui_{adapter,socket}403 — two flavours of the
  #     same 403 regression test.
  #   test/integration/fa_cli_thinking_{abort,livestream_pty} — shared
  #     thinking-stream scaffolding.
  # Baseline entries are keyed on the exact finding message (incl. the
  # jaccard/containment values): ANY drift in a clustered file re-fails
  # the gate and forces a deliberate re-baseline.
  similarity:
    enabled: true
    # 8-token shingles, file-level; 0.5/0.85 are the card's measured
    # operating point (caught every real cluster, no noise).
    jaccard: 0.5
    containment: 0.85
    include: # md docs + dart sources (default is md-only)
      - '**.md'
      - '**.dart'
    exclude:
      # BY-DESIGN twins — excluded via glob per gh-1738 AC2, never
      # baselined (a baseline entry would silently mask edits to them):
      # FlutterFire CLI output and the template it is stamped from —
      # regenerate the real file, never hand-edit either side.
      - 'flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart'
      - 'flutter_app/firebase_options.dart'
      - 'flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart'
      # gen-l10n output: per-locale classes from app_en/app_ru.arb,
      # generated, structurally near-identical by construction.
      - 'flutter_app/lib/l10n/app_localizations_*.dart'
      # Vendored third-party packages — every other gate excludes them
      # (duplication, loc, CRAP); their internal duplication is
      # upstream's business, not this repo's corpus.
      - 'vendor/**'
      # Generated deploy output (site/ is built from blog/ + templates —
      # regen_assetlinks.sh, check_install_pin.sh guard pieces of it);
      # a near-duplicate of its source is the definition of generated.
      - 'site/**'
      # Installed runtime copies of the bundled prompts/skills sources —
      # the agent runtime loads .fah/skills; the mirror is the feature.
      - '.fah/**'
      # Frozen fixture preserving a RETIRED js-apps skill revision —
      # intentionally an old copy; it must not track the living skill.
      - 'flutter_app/test/fixtures/retired_*.md'
      # Local scratch from the standalone-SDK lane recipe (untracked,
      # never present on CI runners) — kept out so local runs match CI.
      - '.dart-tools/**'
      - '.dart-home/**'

for name in sorted(all_names):
    i = src.find(f'\n{name}(')
    if i < 0: continue
    try:
        j = src.index('{', src.index(')', i))
    except ValueError:
        continue
    depth = 0; k = j
    while k < len(src):
        if src[k] == '{': depth += 1
        elif src[k] == '}':
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0: break
        k += 1
    body = src[j:k]
    cc = 1 + len(re.findall(r'\bif\b|\bcase\b|\?\?|&&|\|\||\bfor\b|\bwhile\b|\bcatch\b|\?\.', body)) + len(re.findall(r':', body))//2
    print(f"{name}: ~CC={cc}")

content.text:
- **IT-4**: full incident replay — the exact 2026-10-22 sequence (mixed boot → two picker picks → message) — asserts closed failure. → AC4
- **REG-1** (property test): for EVERY model entry in EVERY cache/list fixture and EVERY switch path, the post-switch quadruple is coherent or the switch refused — no silent mixed state exists anywhere in the enumerated space. → AC1
- **REG-2**: the incident scenario as a permanent regression test; it must fail on any refactor that reopens cross-provider reuse. → AC4
- **REG-3**: byte-equality of provider name across status line, transcript, and request for every switch-path test. → AC5
- **Merge rule:** the REG suite runs as a dedicated CI job; **a red REG job blocks merge even when all UT/IT are green.** No override.

### Edge / border cases

- **E1 — Provider removed after cache built:** a picker entry whose provider was unconfigured between listing and picking ⇒ refusal naming the missing provider and the reconfigure command; no partial triple applied.
- **E2 — Same model id on two providers:** the pick resolves by provider identity of the entry, not by id string; typed-name ambiguity is reported with a disambiguation prompt, never guessed.
- **E3 — Cross-provider pick with no key for target provider:** the triple switch is refused UP FRONT with `set it with /key set <ENV> <value>` for the TARGET provider — the request is never built (this is the incident's correct behavior).
- **E4 — Restore of a pin whose provider definition was deleted:** G3 halts/repairs loudly; it does not bind endpoint and key from different layers (the boot-mix class).
- **E5 — Roles mid-session:** role notes reported "roles unchanged" during the incident switches; role resolution must go through the same gates, so a role-implied model change cannot bypass G1/G2.

arguments.content:
### What changed
Model-switch coherence gates (gh-1788): every `/model` path (typed, numbered, picker) now resolves the whole provider quadruple — provider record, endpoint, key family, model id — or refuses up front, and the live request-build is gated so a mixed model/key/endpoint triple can never reach a socket. The 2026-10-22 cross-provider incident (copilot endpoint + kimi model + kimi key on one request) now replays as a closed failure.

### Key decisions
- New pure-Dart decision core `lib/src/cli/model_switch_coherence.dart` (public via the barrel): typed-target parse (`@provider/model`), cross-provider refusal (E1 unresolvable provider, E3 missing target key with `/key set` hint), request-build verdict (`requestCoherenceRefusal`), restore-gate verdict (`restoreGateDecision` for G3) — hosts reuse it without the CLI.
- G1 switch paths funnel through one `switchModelCoherently` step in `provider_models.dart`; roles-chain and provider-queue lanes are untouched (each `ModelRef` assembles model+key+stream coherently by construction — E5).
- G2 request-build gate wraps only the catalog stream factory (`provider_model_coherence.dart`, a new `part of agent_cli` file — keeps `provider_commands.dart` under the 2800-line gate); refusals surface as `ErrorEvent` instead of a request. Conservative: only provable mixtures refuse; session-only tokens, OAuth blobs and header-auth never refuse.
- G3 restore gate (`session_commands.dart`): a restored pin whose provider record was deleted halts loudly instead of binding endpoint and key from different layers (E4).
- REG suite has its own required CI leg (`model-switch-reg` in ci.yml, same scope gates/pinned actions as `guards`) — a red REG job blocks merge even with UT/IT green.

### How to verify
```bash
dart analyze lib test
dart test test/cli/model_switch_coherence_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_model_coherence_test.dart
dart test test/cli/   # full affected surface
```

<details><summary>Gate flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CMD["/model target (typed | numbered | picker)"] --> G1["G1 switch plan (model_switch_coherence)"]
  G1 -->|unresolvable provider| R1["refuse: /provider hint (E1)"]
  G1 -->|no target key, legacy wiring| R2["refuse: /key set hint (E3)"]
  G1 -->|ok| APPLY["apply quadruple + session record"]
  APPLY --> REQ["request build"] --> G2["G2 request-build gate"]
  G2 -->|mixed triple| EV["ErrorEvent, zero requests (AC4)"]
  G2 -->|coherent| STREAM["provider stream"]
  RESTORE["session restore pin"] --> G3["G3 restore gate"] -->|deleted provider| HALT["loud halt/repair (E4)"]
```

</details>

arguments.text: Dart null-aware map elements: `{?k: v}` conditionally includes the entry based on the KEY (the map key becomes `k` itself), while `{'LITERAL': ?v}` conditions on the VALUE keeping a fixed key. When silencing the `use_null_aware_elements` lint (which flags `if (x != null) 'KEY': x`), the mechanical fix `?x: x` silently RENAMES the map key from 'KEY' to x's value — the map then misses the expected key and downstream lookups return null (symptom: tests hang waiting for an env/key lookup that never resolves). Correct form: `'KEY': ?x`.
